utterance: Hi Chloe, I'm Dr Smith. I see you've come in today with some burning when passing urine. Can you tell me more about what's been happening since yesterday?
reply: It started yesterday morning, so it has been about a day and a half now. It really stings and burns, especially right at the end, just like my last one. I am going constantly, about every half hour, and have to rush even though only a little bit comes out, and I noticed it looks a bit cloudy and smells, though thankfully there is no blood.

awards.label: How long the symptoms have been present
Colour of the urine or any visible blood

utterance: That sounds really uncomfortable. Have you noticed any fevers, chills, nausea, or pain in your lower tummy, back, or sides?
reply: No fevers or shivers, and I'm eating normally and haven't been sick. I just have a low ache above my bladder, and nothing in my back.

utterance: Have you noticed any vaginal discharge, itching, or soreness, or any pain during sex? And is there any chance you might be pregnant?
reply: No, I haven't had any discharge, itching, or soreness, and pain during sex has never been a problem for me either. I don't think there is any chance I'm pregnant, especially since I take the pill.

utterance: Good to know. You mentioned this feels like a urine infection you've had before—how often have you had them, and when was the last one? Also, are you sexually active at the moment, or have you had any new partners recently?
reply: I only had one of these about two years ago, and that is it. I do have a boyfriend I have been with for about a year, and it is just him.

utterance: When was your last normal period, and have you ever had any kidney problems, diabetes, or other medical conditions? Do you take any other medications besides the contraceptive pill, or have any allergies?
reply: My last period was about two weeks ago and it was normal, and I haven't had any kidney problems, diabetes, or other conditions. I only take the pill and I am not allergic to anything that I know of.

finding: Soft. Mild suprapubic tenderness; non-tender elsewhere. No masses or organomegaly.
Soft abdomen. Mild suprapubic tenderness. No guarding or rebound. No masses.
No renal angle tenderness on either side.

result: Leucocytes ++, nitrites positive, blood trace, protein trace. hCG not tested.

utterance: Thanks Chloe. Your examination looks reassuring—your temperature, heart rate, and blood pressure are all normal, and there's no tenderness over your kidneys in your back, just mild tenderness over your bladder. The urine dipstick test here in the room also shows clear signs of a simple bladder infection (acute uncomplicated cystitis). Just to check, what did you take for your last urine infection, and have you taken any antibiotics in the last three months?
reply: I am not sure what I took last time, but I have not had any antibiotics this year.

awards.label: Antibiotics in the last few months
First-line antibiotic: nitrofurantoin 100 mg 6-hourly for 5 days, fosfomycin 3 g once, or trimethoprim 300 mg daily for 3 days

utterance:
I have written a script for trimethoprim 300 mg, which you take as one tablet at night for 3 days. Because this is a straightforward first-time bladder infection in two years and you have no signs of a kidney infection, we don't need to send the urine away to the lab today unless your symptoms don't clear up.

To help with the stinging and discomfort while the antibiotics kick in, you can keep well hydrated by drinking plenty of water, take simple pain relief like paracetamol or ibuprofen, and you can also get urinary alkalinisers (like Ural sachets) over the counter from the pharmacy. This antibiotic won't interfere with your oral contraceptive pill unless you have severe vomiting or diarrhoea.

Your symptoms should start improving within 48 hours and resolve completely within a few days. Please come back to see me if your symptoms haven't improved after 48 hours or don't fully clear after finishing the tablets so we can send a urine sample for testing. Also, if you develop a fever, chills, nausea or vomiting, back or side pain, or feel much more unwell at any point, please seek urgent medical care as that can be a sign the infection is spreading to the kidneys. Do you have any questions about this plan?
reply: No, I don't have any questions, I just really need to get that script so I can get back to work at the café.
